deep.reconstruction:
Context: the page sits between computer printouts dated April 1982, so it predates or coincides with the start of Pursuing Stacks (1983). It is a sketch of the theory of what are now called cofibrantly generated weak factorization systems.

Setting and notation. M is a category and Fl(M) its class of arrows. For a class Ψ of arrows, Ψ^* is the class of arrows with the left lifting property ('left Q-orthogonal', Q presumably for Quillen) with respect to Ψ. For a class L, L_* is the class of arrows with the right lifting property against L. A class L is 'left Q-saturated' if L = Ψ^* for some Ψ.

Lemma. A left Q-saturated class L:
- (a) contains the isomorphisms;
- (b) is stable under composition and under cobase change (pushout);
- (c) is stable under arbitrary direct sums (coproducts);
- (d) is stable under transfinite composition. Precisely: given a well-ordered I and a direct system (A_i) with transition maps u_ij in L, continuous at limit ordinals (A_{i0} = colim_{i<i0} A_i), each structure map A_i → B = colim A_i lies in L.

A marginal remark notes that (c) can be dropped because it follows from (a), (b), (d). This is correct: a coproduct of maps is a transfinite composite of pushouts of the individual maps.

Theorem. Let M admit small colimits and be suitably accessible, so that every object is κ-presentable for some κ (in effect, M locally presentable).
- (1) Let L_0 be a small set of arrows and Ψ = (L_0)_*. Let L be a class with L_0 ⊂ L ⊂ \bar L_0 := Ψ^*. If L satisfies (a)–(d), then the pair (L, Ψ) satisfies the factorization condition: every arrow factors as an L-map followed by a Ψ-map. This is Quillen's small object argument: L contains the transfinite composites of pushouts of coproducts of L_0-maps. Hence, by the retract argument, \bar L_0 is the closure of L under retracts. In particular L = \bar L_0 if L is also stable under direct factors (retracts).
- (2) With the same data L_0, L, the class L is saturated (L = \bar L_0) iff it satisfies (a)–(d) and (e) stability under retracts. In that case (L, Ψ) is a Q-orthogonal pair with factorizations, i.e. a weak factorization system.

Final NB. Part (2) presupposes a small L_0 ⊂ L with the same left saturation as L, i.e. L is 'cofibrantly generated'. The 'next step' is to try to remove this hypothesis: is every class satisfying (a)–(e) in such an M generated by a set?

The page thus serves the stack / homotopy project of the Champs notes: producing model-category-like factorization systems on large cocomplete categories.
errors: Nothing substantively wrong. The theorem needs the domains of L_0 to be small (presentable) relative to transfinite composites of L-maps; 'suitably accessible' (locally presentable) secures this, but the hypothesis is only gestured at.
In (1) the parenthetical 'Hence L = \bar L_0' needs retract-closure, as Grothendieck himself flags with the asterisk. Without it one only gets \bar L_0 = retracts of L.
In (d) requiring every A_i → B to be in L is redundant given (b), but harmless.

ideas.what: Classes defined by left lifting property (left Q-orthogonal) are closed under isos, composition, pushout, coproducts, transfinite composition and retracts
ideas.modern_name: saturated class / closure properties of ⊥Ψ (weakly saturated class)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen (Homotopical Algebra, 1967); Bousfield 1977; standard in Hovey 1999, Hirschhorn
ideas.where_published: Possibly discussed in Pursuing Stacks (1983) in connection with Quillen model structures; not verified

ideas.what: Coproduct stability follows from pushout stability plus transfinite composition
ideas.modern_name: standard lemma on weakly saturated classes
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (e.g. Hovey, Model Categories; Lurie HTT A.1.2)

ideas.what: Small object argument in a cocomplete accessible category: a small set L_0 generates a weak factorization system (\bar L_0, L_0^⊥); the saturated class equals the retracts of cell maps
ideas.modern_name: cofibrantly generated weak factorization system / small object argument in locally presentable categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen 1967; Bousfield 1977; Gabriel–Ulmer 1971 (presentability); Beke 2000, J. Smith (combinatorial model categories, c.1998); Adámek–Herrlich–Rosický–Tholen 2002
ideas.where_published: Transfinite small-object-type constructions appear in SGA4 Exp. I §9; not sure Grothendieck published this formulation

ideas.what: Characterization: L is the saturation of a small set iff L satisfies (a)–(e), given a small generating subset
Question of removing the small generating set hypothesis: is every class closed under (a)–(e) in a locally presentable category the saturation of a set?
ideas.modern_name: cofibrant generation of saturated classes / weak factorization systems in locally presentable categories (relates to Vopěnka-principle results of Adámek–Rosický and Rosický–Tholen)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly sets as 'next step' removing the hypothesis that the saturated class is generated by a small set, i.e. asking whether every class satisfying (a)–(e) in an accessible cocomplete category is cofibrantly generated. Later literature treats such questions, typically needing set-theoretic hypotheses such as Vopěnka's principle. This is not new mathematics, but documents that he posed the question c.1982.
missed.quote: NB. In 2, there was the preliminary assumption of existence of L_0 ⊂ L s.th. L_0 and L have the same left Q-saturations, with L_0 small. Next step is to try to get rid of this.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: shows Grothendieck independently developing combinatorial weak factorization systems in locally presentable/accessible categories c.1982, about 15 years before J. Smith/Beke's combinatorial model categories. Mathematically the question is now understood, with answers sensitive to large-cardinal axioms.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, essentially standard material (small object argument, saturated classes, cofibrant generation) placed in a locally presentable/accessible setting. The early date (1982) and the explicit question about removing the smallness hypothesis are of historical interest, but nothing here is mathematically new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Item c) most likely reads 'L stable under arbitrary direct sums' (coproducts), not 'products'.
Item b) reads 'L stable under composition and cobase change (including "finite")' or similar, i.e. pushouts, not 'also [?] change'.
Left margin NB near c) seems to say c) follows from the others, e.g. 'NB b), d) ⇒ c)'.
Lower margin note reads roughly: 'We need L_0 to be small. We may ignore c) (which follows from a) b) d)); in presence of a), b), d) [c)] is ... stability under cobase change...'.

In ② the phrase reads 'In order that L be saturated (same data L_0, L), it is n.s. that L satisfy conditions a) b) c) d) and e) stability by direct factors'; 'factorization holds for the Q-orthogonal pair (L, Ψ)'.
